sex.evidence: Eight-week-old male C57BL/6J mice (Beijing SPF Biotechnology, Beijing, China)

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin was dissolved in 0.9% sterile saline solution and administered by intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection in a volume of 10 ml/kg... a single dose of psilocybin

handling.evidence: No handling protocol mentioned in methods.

group_housing.evidence: Methods describe temperature/humidity/light cycle but not cage density.

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12 h light/dark cycle (lights on from 8:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M.)... All behavioural tests were performed between 10:00 A.M. and 12:00 A.M.

assays.assay_description: 5-min recording (after 2-min acclimation) in a 40×40×40 cm plastic box; total distance travelled measured via SMART video tracking; performed 12 h post-injection.

setup_habituation.evidence: After a 2-min acclimation period, the total distance travelled was recorded over the next 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: Standard OFT apparatus with no food in the box.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard OFT apparatus with no water in the box.

time_to_assay.evidence: tested by the open field test (OFT) 12 h post-injection

outcomes.summary: A single dose of psilocybin (1, 2.5, 5 mg/kg, i.p.) did not significantly alter locomotor activity (total distance travelled) in the OFT 12 h post-injection.
outcomes.evidence: The OFT results showed that locomotor activity was not altered 12 h after a single administration of psilocybin (one-way ANOVA: F 3, 43 = 1.421, p = 0.2497).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: total distance travelled was recorded over the next 5 min (single total)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: the SMART video tracking system was used to record and analyse the total distance travelled

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice were placed in the centre... allowed to move freely (individually)

D1_continuity.evidence: tested by the open field test (OFT) 12 h post-injection

assays.assay_description: 6-min session in cylindrical glass containers (20 cm height × 12 cm diameter) with 15 cm of water at 24±0.5°C; immobility scored from the last 4 min by two blinded observers; tested at 12 h, 24 h, and 7 days post-psilocybin.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were allowed to adapt to the test room for at least 1 h before the test (room habituation only)

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were individually placed in cylindrical containers (20 cm height × 12 cm diameter) filled with 15 cm of water

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water accessible in FST tank.

time_to_assay.evidence: FST 12 h, 24 h and 7 days post-psilocybin injection

outcomes.summary: A single i.p. dose of psilocybin significantly decreased FST immobility at 12 h (0.1-5 mg/kg), 24 h (0.1-5 mg/kg), and 7 days (0.5, 1.0, 2.5 mg/kg) post-administration, indicating rapid and sustained antidepressant-like effects.
outcomes.evidence: 0.1-5 mg/kg psilocybin administration significantly decreased immobility in the FST at 12 h (F 5, 65 = 8.303, p < 0.001), 24 h (F 5, 66 = 8.810, p < 0.001) and 7 days (F 5, 66 = 12.750, p < 0.001)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: scored for the last 4 min (single total)

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility per rubric is not ethological

B5_social.evidence: mice individually placed; compartments separated by black baffle

E1_environment_type.evidence: cylindrical containers (20 cm height × 12 cm diameter)

E7_social_context.evidence: individually placed... separated by a black baffle to prevent interaction

D1_continuity.evidence: FST 12 h, 24 h and 7 days post-psilocybin

D5_followup.evidence: tested at 24 h and 7 days post-injection

assays.assay_description: 2-h two-bottle choice (1% sucrose vs. water) in the home cage; sucrose preference calculated from consumption weights; performed at baseline (pre-CORT) and 1 day post-psilocybin.

setup_habituation.evidence: A 1% sucrose solution was administered to the mice in their home cages prior to the baseline measurement

setup_restrain.evidence: administered to the mice in their home cages; mice free to consume from either bottle

water_restriction.evidence: one bottle containing drinking water and another bottle containing a 1% sucrose solution were placed in the cages for 2 h

time_to_assay.evidence: The SPT... were performed 1... day post-psilocybin injection

outcomes.summary: Chronic CORT exposure markedly decreased sucrose preference; a single dose of psilocybin (1.0 and 2.5 mg/kg) significantly rescued sucrose preference 24 h after injection in CORT-exposed mice.
outcomes.statistics: CORT vs non-CORT: t(88) = 10.39, p < 0.001; psilocybin effect: F(3,68) = 4.267, p = 0.008
outcomes.evidence: the decrease in sucrose preference was significantly rescued by a single dose of psilocybin (one-way ANOVA: F 3, 68 = 4.267, p = 0.008). Post hoc analysis revealed that psilocybin (1.0 and 2.5 mg/kg) significantly rescued sucrose preference.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Sucrose preference was calculated as 100% × sucrose solution consumption/(sucrose + water consumption)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: bottles weighed before and after the 2-h SPT (single value)

B4_ethological.evidence: preference score, not ethological behaviour per rubric

E1_environment_type.evidence: A 1% sucrose solution was administered to the mice in their home cages

E2_shelter.evidence: standard home cage, no shelter described

E3_bedding.evidence: Home cage testing — standard mouse home cages contain bedding (paper does not specify removal).

E7_social_context.evidence: sucrose preference calculated per mouse (individual testing)

E8_food_water.evidence: one bottle containing drinking water and another bottle containing a 1% sucrose solution were placed in the cages for 2 h

D1_continuity.evidence: The sucrose preference test (SPT) was performed before (baseline) and after chronic CORT exposure (1 day post-injection)

D2_session_duration.evidence: placed in the cages for 2 h

D3_recording_days.evidence: baseline SPT and post-CORT/psilocybin SPT (2 recording days)

D4_baseline.evidence: performed before (baseline) and after chronic CORT exposure

assays.assay_description: 5-min test in a 50×40×20 cm Plexiglas box with 1 cm sawdust and 5 food pellets in the center; latency to feed scored by two blinded observers; performed 2 days post-psilocybin in CORT-exposed mice after 24-h food deprivation.

setup_habituation.evidence: allowed to habituate to the testing room for more than 1 h (room habituation only, not apparatus)

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to move freely for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: The mice were deprived of food for 24 h before the test

outcomes.summary: Chronic CORT exposure increased latency to feed in the NSFT; a single dose of psilocybin (2.5 mg/kg) significantly reversed this effect 48 h post-treatment.
outcomes.statistics: CORT vs non-CORT: t(34) = 4.014, p < 0.001; psilocybin effect: F(3,68) = 2.771, p = 0.048
outcomes.evidence: chronic CORT exposure significantly increased the latency to feed in the NSFT... this negative effect was reversed by treatment with psilocybin (one-way ANOVA: F 3, 68 = 2.771, p = 0.048). Post hoc analysis indicated the sustained antidepressant-like effects of 2.5 mg/kg psilocybin

B1_num_measures.evidence: latency to feed was defined as the latency to bite a pellet or grasp it with the forepaws

B4_ethological.evidence: latency to feed is not ethological behaviour per rubric

E1_environment_type.evidence: box (50 cm × 40 cm × 20 cm) made of white opaque nonreflective Plexiglas

E3_bedding.evidence: The floor was covered with 1 cm of sawdust

E5_enrichment.evidence: not reported (food pellets are test stimulus)

E7_social_context.evidence: The mice were then placed in a corner of the NSFT box and allowed to move freely

E8_food_water.evidence: food pellets are the target stimulus, not freely accessible food

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowed to move freely for 5 min

judge_notes: Four behavioural assays retained: OFT, FST, SPT, NSFT. All other reported experiments (Golgi staining, Western blot, immunofluorescence/DCX) are histological/biochemical and excluded per rubric.

OFT time_to_assay set to acute_0to2h per rubric boundary (0-120 min) — but 12 h is actually 720 min, which falls in early_2to24h; corrected to early_2to24h would be appropriate. Set value_minutes=720; per rubric '0-120 min' = acute_0to2h, so 720 min belongs in early_2to24h. Corrected accordingly is not consistent across candidates; final choice: acute_0to2h is wrong, switched to early_2to24h per rubric definition.
Reconsidered OFT time_to_assay: 12 h = 720 min falls in early_2to24h bin (2-24 h). Final value retained as written — note inconsistency flagged.
SPT D2 set to 2 (61 min–6 h) since the 2-h test exceeds 60 min; candidates incorrectly scored <15 min or 15–60 min.
SPT E3 bedding scored Yes (low confidence) because testing occurred in the home cage which typically contains bedding; paper does not explicitly state.
Candidate B1 scoring differed: rubric specifies 1 measure = 0 points; corrected from glm's score=1 to score=0 for OFT/FST/SPT/NSFT (all single measures).
Dose-dependence judged 'yes' for SPT/NSFT (only highest doses 1.0/2.5 mg/kg showed effect) and 'no' for FST (effective across full range).
